processing: A cultivar name, not a finished tea, so processing depends on the maker. The breeders report it making both green tea and broken black tea.
harvest_season: Not documented for this cultivar; spring is usually the prized picking for Yunnan green teas.
appearance_dry: Not documented; Yunnan greens typically show sturdy twisted leaf, often with visible down.
appearance_liquor: The breeders report a bright yellow-green liquor when made as green tea, and a vivid red as broken black tea.
appearance_wet: Not documented; Yunnan greens typically open into thick, soft leaf.
taste_profile: No tasting notes are documented for this cultivar; Yunnan greens in general are fuller and more robust than eastern Chinese greens.

brewing.notes: General advice for a Yunnan green; nothing specific to this cultivar is on record.

vintage_note: No sale pattern is documented, and it is rarely if ever named on retail tea. Any green tea made from it would follow the usual pattern of its class: sold as the current year's harvest and drunk within the year.
description:
Yuncha 1 is a tea plant cultivar from Yunnan, selected from a single plant by the province's tea research institute. 'Yun' stands for Yunnan and 'cha' for tea.

It is a tree-type, early-sprouting plant with a half-open habit and glossy, elliptical, deep green leaves. Its breeders report good quality and strong disease resistance, and consider it plantable across most of Yunnan. Do not confuse it with Yuncha Chunyun, a separately described Yunnan cultivar.

As a guide only, Yunnan greens tend to be fuller and more robust than those from eastern China, and they take slightly hotter water. No tasting notes specific to this cultivar are at hand.

If you see this name on a tea, ask the seller for the grower and the picking date, since the cultivar name alone tells you very little.
history: Yuncha 1 was described in a 2009 paper by Tian Yiping and colleagues at the Tea Research Institute of the Yunnan Academy of Agricultural Sciences, as a selection from a single plant. Its parent stock and spread are not established here, and it does not appear to be a tea drinkers commonly seek out by name.
